\caption{The tiered adaptive controller against comparators whose threshold or dose was tuned on held-out patients (all settings, including the controller's own threshold $\omega$, chosen on the even-numbered patients and evaluated on the odd-numbered ones, $n = 500$ each). Entries: survival of the tiered controller minus the comparator, in percentage points, with 95\% paired-bootstrap confidence interval; the tuned setting is given below each entry. Positive values favor the tiered controller. PRN (\emph{pro re nata}): a dose when at least the given number of seizures was counted in the preceding 8 or 24~h, or when the extended Kalman filter (EKF) rate exceeds the threshold. Tiered, 24-h average: the same dose tiers driven by a 24-hour moving average of counts instead of the EKF. Sz: seizure harm; Drug: drug harm. A tuned fixed dose beats the tiered controller in High Sz / Low Drug and Low Sz / Low Drug; when the drug is harmful, rules that rarely dose (PRN, no treatment) match or beat it.}
